newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says EU may set terms on Boeing merger.
newsitem.headline: Germany says EU may set terms on Boeing merger.

text.p: Germany said Tuesday the European Commission might set conditions for the proposed merger between Boeing Co. and McDonnell Douglas Corp.

A report by Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said the creation of a combined U.S. plane maker with revenues of $48 billion increased the pressure on Europe's fragmented aircraft sector to consolidate in order to compete.

The merger, valued at more than $15 billion, has not yet been reported either to Brussels or to Germany's cartel office, but this is expected to take place either in late January or early February, the report said.

If the Commission is responsible, as appears likely, it will probably not block the merger. But, the report added, EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert has already indicated that "terms and conditions" could be set.
The report, reviewed by Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet Tuesday, did not elaborate. But it noted that Boeing's revenues exceeded thresholds activating Brussels' competence in competition regulation.
